scenes.say: Ever wondered how Docker containers find each other, or how your app gets traffic from outside? Let’s break down Docker networking and ports.

scenes.label: Bridge
scenes.sub: Each container gets a private I.P. address.
scenes.say: By default, Docker puts containers on a bridge network. Each one gets a private I.P. address, isolated from others.

scenes.label: UserNet
scenes.sub: User networks add DNS—containers use names.
scenes.say: Create a user-defined network, and Docker gives you DNS. Now containers can reach each other by name, not just by I.P.

scenes.title: Expose your app
scenes.say: To let outside traffic in, publish a port. Dash p, host port, colon, container port. Traffic to host port 8080 goes to your app inside.

scenes.question: What does -p 8080:80 do?
scenes.right: Maps host port 8080 to container port 80.
scenes.say: Watch out: dash p eight zero eight zero colon eighty maps host port 8080 to port 80 inside your container, not the other way around.
